text:
ashley: heads-up — weird spike in pending tiny-gang pods in us-west2 (rack3). Seeing repeated soft-evict cycles. I think NIC p95 latency is causing the scheduler to prefer spreading instead of binpacking, leaving lots of 0.5–2 GPU fragments. :warning:

matt: can you paste `kubectl get pods -o wide` for a couple of pending ones?

ashley: sure — sample:```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | egrep 'pending|evicted'
model-train-7c9 Pending 0/1 0.5 GPU nodeAffinity=preferred ... <none>
mini-gang-1 Pending 0/1 1 GPU nodeAffinity=required ... <none>
...
```

ashley: nodes show many `warmpool-*` with taint `gpu/warmpool:NoSchedule` but their NIC p95 jumped to ~250ms around the same time we saw spreading.

leo: that matches something we saw last month — when interconnect latency spikes, scheduler scoring penalizes node-interconnect hotspots so pods spread to lower-scoring nodes instead of filling racks. That increases fragmentation.

sarah: quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily lower topologySpread weight / anti-affinity for tiny-gang pods, 2) untaint a subset of warm-pool nodes so scheduler has safe compact targets, 3) run descheduler job to compact after latency subsides.

jordan: i'm +1 on descheduler but do a dry-run first. If we evict during a latency window we might worsen tail latency for running jobs.

ashley: agreed. Plan I'm about to run:
- patch Deployment affinity from `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` -> `preferred` for tiny-gang test set
- untaint `warmpool-*-rack3` for 20m via:
```
kubectl patch node warmpool-3-02 -p '{"spec":{"taints":[]}}'
```
- dry-run descheduler: `descheduler --policy-file=compact-policy.yaml --dry-run`

matt: run the dry-run and paste results here please.

ashley: dry-run output snippets:
```
I0312 12:34:05 descheduler: candidate evictions 58, would compact into 14 nodes (score delta > 20)
most candidates = tiny-gang-* (gpu=0.5,1)
```

sre-bot: created incident INF-2345: "us-west2 rack3 scheduler spread causing GPU fragmentation" assigned to eng-platform. Priority=P3.

deploy-bot: starting rollout: scheduler-configmap patch (set topologyWeightDefaults: reduce anti-affinity to 50) — canary on us-west2 only.

leo: FYI lower topologyWeight helped last time. Also watch NVLink / pci errors; sometimes the scheduler sees NIC errors as node NotReady briefly which makes things worse.

jordan: if compact succeeds we should expect ~12–18% GPU-hour reduction for batch workloads (estimate from prior run). Keep an eye on cost dashboards.

ashley: applying untaint + canary patches now. I'll monitor pod churn and latency. If evictions > 200 in 10m we roll back.

matt: noted. I'll keep the alert rule on `eviction_rate` and `gpu_utilization_skew` at hand.

ashley: update — after untaint + scheduler patch: 10m in, pending queue dropped by 70%, fragmentation heatmap shows a lot of small slots coalescing. NIC p95 normalized to ~40ms.

sarah: great. schedule a follow-up to make this config change conditional in autoscaler: only relax spread if interconnect p95 < 100ms, so we avoid flipping during unstable windows.

ashley: good idea. filing follow-up RFC. For now leaving the canary for 2h and will promote if stable. :thumbsup:
